text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a cascade yesterday when we drained two GPU nodepools in eu-west during the maintenance window. Cold-start QPS spike + billing jump.

maria: Ugh. Can you paste the sequence? Was it autoscaler-triggered or explicit drain?

alex: Autoscaler + nodepool rolling update (taint+evict). Pattern was: cordon -> evict -> drain; multiple AZs drained in parallel. CA reacted and spawned nodes, which then triggered more evictions because some pods couldn't reschedule fast enough.

sam: Sounds like a classic cascade. Did pods hit PDBs or pending due to node selectors / scarce GPU SKU?

alex: A mix. Some pods were blocked by PDBs, others by nodeAffinities for A100-only pools. Also saw preemptible nodes disappearing mid-evict which made it worse.

jia: Suggestion: limit concurrent node drains per nodepool/AZ and add a per-pool cooldown window. That way CA won't try to replace everything at once.

katie: Agree. Also we should prefer draining non-critical workloads first (batch, offline) and respect a preservation priority for realtime-serving pods.

maria: Can we implement rate-limiting at the nodepool controller level? Like `maxDrainsPerMinute` and `cooldownSeconds`?

alex: Yep. Drafted a config prototype — what do you think?

```
# nodepool-drain-config ConfigMap
maxDrainsPerMinute: 2
cooldownSeconds: 300
priorityClasses:
  - realtime
  - high
  - default
```

sam: That's reasonable. Also we need a circuit-breaker: if pending pod count spikes > X, pause drains and notify. Otherwise we just postpone and cause OOMs.

jia: We should also surface the metric `nodepool.drain_rate` and alert when it crosses threshold + pending GPU pods > 5 for >5m.

katie: How does this interact with scale-to-zero for dev pools? Dev pools are allowed to go to 0. We don't want rate-limits preventing scale-to-zero when it's supposed to.

alex: For dev pools we can have an override flag `allowImmediateScaleToZero=true`. Only prod/dedicated pools get rate limits.

maria: Edge case: preemptible instances get reclaimed faster than we can drain. For those, add a preemption handler: when the cloud notifies of imminent preemption, immediately cordon but limit evictions to low-priority pods first.

sam: Can we reuse the existing drain-queue concept from the k8s-ops repo? Just add throttling and per-AZ fairness.

alex: Yes — plan: implement a small controller that batches drain requests, enforces per-AZ concurrency, implements exponential backoff on failures, and emits metrics for observability. I'll prototype this week.

maria: +1. Add an integration test that simulates AZ-wide drain and measures cold-start token delta and cost delta.

infra-bot: Deploy plan created: `drain-throttle-controller:v0.1.0-canary` targeted to staging eu-west-1a. CI job: `integration/drain-throttle/sim`.

katie: Who owns rollout and alert thresholds? I can take owner and create the SLO/alert PR.

alex: Thanks — assign to katie for alerting and to sam for controller review. I'll do the prototype and tests.

maria: Follow-ups: 1) add nodepool-level config CRD 2) add `nodepool.drain_rate` metric + dashboard 3) add cost runbook entry for warmup/coldstart spikes.

sam: Quick note: make sure Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) have an opt-out so we never accidentally scale them to zero.

alex: Good call. We'll add `scaleToZeroAllowed: false` on reserved pools by default.

katie: I'll open the alert PR after the canary results. Ping me with the prometheus rule. :thumbsup:

alex: Will do. Thanks everyone.

maria: Nice plan. low risk, measurable.

sam: sgtm

jia: sgtm

infra-bot: Canary deploy succeeded in staging eu-west-1a — no regressions in 2h smoke tests. Logs: `/var/log/drain-throttle/*.log`

alex: Sweet. Next— schedule a small production canary during low traffic window and watch `pending_gpu_pods` and `nodepool.drain_rate`.

katie: Added calendar invite for Fri 03:00 UTC.

alex: Thanks.
